title: Uhud
hook: They were winning. Then a group left their post, and everything turned.

screens.text: **They were winning.** Then a group of his own people left the post he'd told them never to leave, and everything turned. What he did next, and what Allah told him to do, is the real story of Uhud.
**Quraysh come back.** A year after Badr, in **Shawwal** of 3 AH, Quraysh marched on Madinah to avenge their losses and camped by Mount Uhud [IslamQA 11575].
bubbles: The Makkans were about three thousand. The Muslims were far fewer, after about a third of their army turned back with a hypocrite leader [Yaqeen (Hate)].

screens.prompt: You're one of fifty archers on a hill. Your orders: don't leave this spot, win or lose, until he sends for you. The enemy is running. Your friends below are gathering what they left behind. What do you do?

options.text: Stay at the post, as he ordered
options.feedback: Right. A few did stay. But most ran down, and the battle turned [Bukhari 3039; Q 3:152].
That's what most did, despite their commander reminding them of the order. Then the battle turned [Bukhari 3039].
Not quite. The order already covered this: win or lose, stay until he sends for you [Bukhari 3039].

screens.text: **The battle turns.** When most of the archers left, the battle turned against the Muslims. The Prophet ﷺ was wounded: a tooth broken and his head cut. He wondered aloud how a people could succeed after wounding their own prophet [Muslim 1791].
bubbles: Allah answered: *"Not for you, [O Muhammad, but for Allah], is the decision"* [Q 3:128, Saheeh Intl.]. Their fate was Allah's to decide, not his.

screens.text: A hard day, and what came after.

events.title: Pardon and consult
events.text: Allah tells him to be gentle with them, forgive them and keep consulting them [Q 3:159].

screens.text: **What Allah told him next.** His own people had disobeyed and cost them dearly. The Qur'an praised his gentleness and told him: *"So pardon them and ask forgiveness for them and consult them in the matter"* [Q 3:159, Saheeh Intl.].

screens.before: "So pardon them and ask forgiveness for them and

options.feedback: Yes. After a failure caused by their choices, he was told to keep asking their opinion.
Not quite. The opposite: pardon them, pray for them, and keep consulting them.
Not quite. He kept the same people and kept consulting them.

cards.back: The Prophet's ﷺ beloved uncle was killed at Uhud by a man named Wahshi [Bukhari 4072].
Wahshi became Muslim and came to the Prophet ﷺ. He was accepted [Bukhari 4072].
He asked Wahshi to keep out of his sight. Forgiving doesn't mean the grief disappears [Bukhari 4072].

screens.text: **Forgive, and keep them close.** After a loss his own people caused, he forgave them and kept asking their advice. He even accepted his uncle's killer as a Muslim. You can forgive and still feel the hurt. Day 77 talked about grief.

screens.situation: Tyler organised the masjid's first open house for non-Muslim neighbours. Two volunteers didn't show, and it went badly. Next month, he's planning another.

options.text: Forgive them, talk it through, and still ask their ideas for next time
options.feedback: Yes. That's Uhud's lesson: pardon, pray for them, and keep consulting them.

options.text: Do the next one alone so nobody lets him down
options.feedback: Not quite. After Uhud, he was told to keep consulting the same people, not to shut them out.

options.text: Call them out in the group chat
options.feedback: Not quite. Public blame breaks people. Talk privately and kindly, like his gentleness in Q 3:159.

check.prompt: What turned the battle of Uhud?

options.text: Most of the archers left the post he had told them to hold
options.feedback: Right. They left when the enemy fled, and the battle turned [Bukhari 3039].

options.text: The Muslims ran out of food
options.feedback: Not quite. It was the archers leaving their post, against his clear order.

check.prompt: After Uhud, what did Allah tell him to do with his Companions?

options.text: Pardon them and keep consulting them

options.feedback: Not quite. Q 3:159 told him to pardon them, pray for them and consult them.

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- A year after Badr, in Shawwal 3 AH, Quraysh came to avenge Badr and camped by Mount Uhud [IslamQA 11575]. (scholar question Q39)
- The Makkans were about 3,000; the Muslims about 700 after a third of the army withdrew with the hypocrite 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy (single source; say "about") [Yaqeen (How Muhammad Confronted Hate)].
- He placed fifty archers on a hill under 'Abdullah ibn Jubayr and told them not to leave, win or lose, until he sent for them; when the enemy fled, most left despite their commander reminding them of the order, and the battle turned [Bukhari 3039; Q 3:152].
- He was wounded (a tooth broken, his head cut) and wondered how a people could succeed who did this to their prophet; Q 3:128 was revealed [Muslim 1791].
- His uncle Hamzah was killed by Wahshi, who later became Muslim and told the story himself; the Prophet ﷺ asked him to keep out of his sight [Bukhari 4072].
- The Qur'an told him to be gentle, pardon them, ask forgiveness for them and consult them [Q 3:159]; Day 73 and Day 70 use this verse.
- His rules of war applied: no killing of women or children [Bukhari 3015].

**Likely questions**
- *"Why did the archers leave?"* They saw the enemy fleeing and went down for the spoils, though their commander reminded them of the order [Bukhari 3039]. The Qur'an names the disobedience and also says Allah forgave them [Q 3:152].
- *"Wasn't the Prophet ﷺ a warrior?"* Day 71 frame: defence of the community after years of persecution, strict rules [Bukhari 3015]; Uhud was an army coming to Madinah. No rulings on fighting today. (scholar question Q39)
- *"How many died?"* Many Muslims were killed, including Hamzah. Don't dwell on numbers or describe deaths.
- *"How could he forgive Hamzah's killer?"* He accepted Wahshi's Islam; he was also human and asked not to see him. Forgiveness and grief can live together.
- *"What happened to Hamzah's body?"* Say only that he was killed and deeply mourned; don't describe what was done afterwards.

**Escalate:** any question about fighting today (fixed policy).

**Don't**
- Don't describe wounds beyond the hadith's words, killings, or the mutilation reports.
- Don't present Wahshi's story as the Prophet ﷺ being angry or vengeful.
- Don't blame "the Companions" as a whole; it was a group of archers, and Allah forgave them [Q 3:152].
